statement: manifest.json identifies namespace ownership, protocol version, repository identity, and the supported schema dialect.
dossier.json is the sole canonical truth for current governed state.
Only immutable records referenced by the current dossier snapshot affect current state.
Handoff, submission, and decision envelopes are immutable create-once records.
An unreferenced immutable envelope is reported as an orphan and never applied as current truth.
The locks directory is transient coordination state and is never dossier truth or history.
M0 has no authoritative brief.md; every human-readable view is generated from canonical data so Markdown cannot become a second editable truth.
Every identifier-bearing governed schema field uses the shared opaque-string scalar contract.
A compatible re-initialization preserves the repository identifier rather than reusing it for another repository identity.
Dossier identifiers are never reused within one repository.
Run identifiers are never reused within one dossier.
Handoff identifiers are never reused within one dossier.
Submission identifiers are never reused within one dossier.
Decision identifiers are never reused within one dossier.
Criterion identifiers are unique within one dossier.
Evidence identifiers are unique within one dossier.
Operation identifiers form an idempotency scope within one dossier and basis revision.
Reusing an operation identifier at a later basis has no global-deduplication guarantee.
Human-readable titles are display metadata and never identity.
Revisions are non-negative decimal strings with no leading zero except the value 0.
Digests use the exact sha256:<lowercase-hex> wire grammar.
Timestamps use the UTC RFC 3339 wire grammar ending in Z.
Ordering and concurrency never depend on wall-clock time.
Machine fields and error codes remain English ASCII and locale-invariant.
Governed JSON rejects bytes that are not valid UTF-8 before schema validation.
Governed JSON rejects duplicate object member names after JSON escape decoding before schema validation.
Governed JSON rejects isolated Unicode surrogates and Unicode noncharacters before schema validation.
Protocol JSON rejects numeric values and represents counters and revisions with restricted decimal strings.
Governed JSON rejects a byte-order mark unless that artifact contract explicitly permits it.
Every schema uses JSON Schema Draft 2020-12.
Every root schema explicitly declares the Draft 2020-12 dialect and a stable $id.
Protocol version and schema dialect are separate required fields.
Runtime validation resolves only bundled and pinned named root schemas and references, with no network resolution.
Security- and state-critical objects are closed and reject unknown critical fields.
Unknown protocol major versions fail closed.
JSON Schema format, default, and examples annotations are never the sole validity or authorization mechanism.
Canonical bytes are UTF-8 RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme bytes of an explicitly named projection.
Canonical projection bytes are hashed as a sha256:<lowercase-hex> SHA-256 wire digest.
Canonicalization preserves array order.
JCS does not normalize Unicode, so NFC and NFD strings remain distinct.
State revision, state digest, content digest, observed-evidence digest, checks digest, and submission digest remain six distinct protocol concepts.
The dossier-state projection contains every canonical dossier field except state_digest and invents no other exclusion.
The content projection contains exactly dossier ID, objective, scope, constraints, ordered criteria, and ordered evidence with every declared field except captured_at.
The observed-evidence projection contains exactly the specified root and evidence-result fields.
Observed-evidence results preserve dossier evidence order.
Observed-evidence stable limitation codes use ASCII lexical order.
Observed-evidence projection excludes absolute paths, platform errors, timestamps, localized messages, retry counts, and filesystem enumeration order.
External references and human observations project human_review_required with null observed artifact digest and size.
The checks projection contains exactly the specified root and result fields.
Check invariant results use protocol-stage order and then ASCII code order.
Check criterion results and supporting evidence IDs preserve their canonical dossier order.
Check stable warning codes use ASCII lexical order.
Checks projection excludes revision, state digest, envelope pointers, last-operation, OS error, path, time, localization, and diagnostic metadata.
Checks fail when any invariant fails.
Checks fail when a mechanical criterion lacks current mechanical evidence.
Checks fail when a recorded-human criterion lacks linked evidence.
human_review_required alone neither fails mechanical checks nor asserts substantive approval.
Assignment, locks, display timestamps, orphan records, and filesystem observations do not change content_digest.
Adding a registered evidence record changes content_digest.
Changed artifact bytes stale dependent envelopes through observations without silently changing stored revision or content_digest.
The manifest contains exactly the specified protocol, protocol version, schema dialect, repository ID, and creation timestamp fields.
The dossier snapshot contains the complete specified brief, revision, self-digest, last-operation, active-run, evidence, and current-envelope-pointer fields.
Evidence records use a closed kind-tagged shape and require artifact digest and size for local file and captured command-result artifacts.

Local evidence paths use slash-separated repository-relative lexical spelling and reject absolute, drive, UNC, backslash, empty, dot, dot-dot, NUL, ADS, device-alias, and trailing-dot-or-space forms without lowercasing.
Filesystem validation proves repository-root containment, exact segment resolution, and rejects ambiguous filesystem aliases including hardlinks.
Filesystem validation rejects symlinks, junctions, and unsupported reparse-point escapes.
M0 mechanically validates local file and captured command-result evidence; external references and human observations remain human-review data and cannot satisfy mechanical criteria.
All acceptance criteria are conjunctive.
One current linked local artifact mechanically satisfies a mechanical criterion.
Multiple artifacts linked to one criterion are alternatives, so one current qualifying artifact is sufficient.
A recorded-human criterion requires linked evidence, remains human_review_required, and is never declared substantively true by mechanical checks.
A submission contains exactly the specified digest-bound fields.
The submission self-projection excludes only submission_digest before computing that digest.
Submission creation is legal only with passing checks, the active submitting run, and no current unaccepted handoff.
Submission publication advances revision, sets current_submission_id, and clears current_decision_id.
Decision recording retains the current submission pointer.
A content change retains the existing submission and decision pointers so their staleness remains visible.
A new submission replaces current_submission_id and clears current_decision_id.
A handoff transition alone preserves current_submission_id and current_decision_id.
Checks, review, acceptance, and handoff states are derived and are never stored as a free-standing DONE field or mutable checks cache.
check, show, and submission creation recompute current checks from canonical state and present evidence observations.
ready_for_review requires a referenced submission whose covered content, observations, and checks still match.
accepted requires a referenced acceptance decision for the still-current submission digest.
Covered-content change stales dependent submissions, unaccepted handoffs, and decisions.
Rejection derives changes_requested.
A later submission is a new immutable envelope rather than a mutation of an earlier submission.
M0 exposes no dossier abandonment transition.
M0 exposes no dossier archival or reopening transition.
M0 exposes no dossier deletion or purge transition.
Material brief changes require a new dossier.
Every governed mutation creates the dossier writer guard with an exclusive-create primitive before reading current state.
After guard acquisition, every governed mutation reads the current snapshot.
The current snapshot loaded under the writer guard is schema- and state-validated before transition.
After guard acquisition, every governed mutation compares exact expected revision, state digest, and operation identity.
Every governed mutation constructs and validates one complete next snapshot before publication.
Snapshot publication creates its temporary file in the target directory.
Snapshot publication flushes and closes the staged temporary according to the declared profile.
Snapshot publication uses one declared profile replacement primitive.
A governed mutation reopens and validates the published snapshot.
A governed mutation releases the writer guard only after published-snapshot verification.
An identical immediate retry scoped to dossier, basis revision, and operation ID returns the prior success without another transition.
Replaying an older operation after a later transition returns conflict.
Reusing a same-basis operation ID with different input fails.
A writer lock records guard ID, exact basis revision and digest, creation time, and declared-profile process identity.
Lock age means only possibly stale and never authorizes automatic takeover.
Guard recovery first obtains a separate create-exclusive recovery guard.
A held recovery guard visibly excludes ordinary writers and every second recovery attempt.
Guard recovery requires an exact interactive confirmation and profile-proven prior-process termination.
Confirmed recovery quarantines the old lock, revalidates state, and publishes a guarded no-op revision.
Recovery exclusivity is released only after verification.
Recovery stops with recovery-required when prior-writer termination is live, unavailable, or inconclusive.
The exactly-one-writer guarantee resumes only after proven termination and completed profile-specific recovery.
Handoff, submission, and decision publication acquires the writer guard before reading current state.
Envelope publication validates transition and check preconditions after guard acquisition and before immutable-envelope creation.
Envelope publication creates the immutable envelope with an operation-derived ID.
Envelope publication validates the created envelope and its digest before pointer publication.
Envelope publication atomically replaces the snapshot so it references the envelope.
Envelope publication verifies referenced state before releasing the writer guard.
A crash before pointer publication may leave an orphan envelope, but the orphan has no authority over current state.
Envelope IDs derive from operation IDs.
The first envelope create attempt fixes every persisted ID and timestamp.
An identical retry reuses and validates persisted envelope values and input bytes.
A conflicting immutable envelope with the same ID fails closed.
A handoff envelope contains exactly the specified offer fields.
Handoff envelopes store no status or status-basis member; offer status is derived.
Only the active run can create a handoff offer.
Creating a handoff records an offer but does not transfer active responsibility.
The offer binds the validated pre-offer revision and digest, deterministic next published revision, and offered content digest without self-referential snapshot digest.
Acceptance must match intended actor, exact published revision, offered content digest, active run, current handoff pointer, and independently validated current state-digest precondition.
Successful acceptance creates the recipient run and atomically updates active actor, run ID, and started-by-handoff pointer; the previous run immediately loses write authority.
Before acceptance, later governed mutation that changes a required acceptance precondition makes the offer stale.
M0 has no handoff cancellation operation or cancellation history.
Actor labels are recorded claims and never authenticated identities.
Accepted handoff is derived only from matching current handoff, started-by-handoff, recipient actor, and a valid immutable offer.
Successful acceptance is terminal for its handoff envelope.
Ordinary governed work after acceptance does not retroactively stale the accepted handoff.
A later handoff replaces the current handoff reference.
check is read-only and never advances state_revision.
check reports parsing, schema/version, cross-file, evidence-safety, evidence-integrity, envelope-integrity, digest, and derived-status stages distinctly.
Submission creation reruns current checks after acquiring the writer guard.
No mutable checks result is stored in the dossier snapshot.
A submission embeds the current content, observed-evidence, and checks digests.
Later show and check recompute current evidence observations from canonical state.
Later show and check compare recomputed observations with the referenced submission to derive currentness.
A validator exception is an internal error and can never produce a valid result.
Local artifact validation uses open-read-validate-close.
Local artifact validation rejects outside-root evidence paths.
Passing checks claim only the declared machine-checkable invariants, not usefulness, correctness, quality, or acceptance.
TOCTOU risk outside the validated handle and non-cooperating filesystem changes remain a documented limitation.
Local artifact validation rejects symbolic links, junctions, and unsupported reparse points.
Local artifact validation rejects a directory where a regular artifact file is required.
Local artifact validation rejects an empty artifact when empty evidence is disallowed.
Local artifact validation reports a missing artifact without opening an alias.
Local artifact validation reports artifact bytes that no longer match the registered digest and size.
An acceptance or rejection envelope contains exactly the specified closed fields.
A decision binds one exact submission digest and uses identity_assurance recorded-interactive-claim.
criteria_reviewed exactly equals the submitted dossier's complete criterion-ID list in canonical criterion order; partial acceptance is unavailable.
A decision is legal only for the snapshot's exact current submission ID and digest; older or non-current submissions fail even when covered digests happen to match.
Every decision requires an interactive display of the exact submission, criteria, and explicit confirmation phrase.
No --yes or non-interactive decision path exists.
Orphan decision recovery repeats the exact interactive display and confirmation before pointer update.
Decision output consistently says Recorded Human Acceptance rather than authenticated approval, attestation, or non-repudiation.
Recorded interactive decision identity is not strong authentication and may be impersonated by a program controlling the terminal.
The reference CLI exposes only the eleven specified M0 commands plus its version request.
Dossier creation creates the initial active run for the recorded actor with a null started-by-handoff pointer.
Every dossier-scoped command requires an explicit dossier ID and M0 never guesses a current, recent, or sole dossier.
Every mutation requires an operation ID.
Every existing-dossier mutation in machine mode requires exact expected revision and state digest.
Human mode may omit a basis only after the same invocation displays and confirms the complete basis and intended transition.
After human confirmation, guarded comparison remains bound to the displayed basis and never silently rebinds after intervening state.
After --json is detected, every normal result is exactly one result envelope on stdout.
In JSON mode stderr contains no machine-required information and warnings remain structured.
Machine consumers branch on stable symbolic code and process exit, independent of localized message.
Every stable symbolic result code maps to its specified process-exit class, and exact callers inspect the symbolic code.
No error recommends destructive deletion as its default remediation.
dossier show presents the bounded specified current material.
dossier show reports unresolved proof limitations and exactly one recommended next valid action.
JSON mode exposes the complete structured current view.
Default human current view remains bounded and points to deeper data instead of embedding large evidence.
Repository-root discovery starts at the current directory and resolves the owning version-control worktree when available.
Initialization displays the resolved repository root before mutation.
Initialization creates only .case-agent and changes no byte outside that namespace.
Existing incompatible, partial, linked, junctioned, or unknown .case-agent content fails closed as a collision before writes.
Repeating the same compatible initialization is byte-idempotent.
An unsupported newer major namespace remains read-only inspectable and is never modified.
M0 initialization never modifies .gitignore, host instructions, hooks, PATH, or user-global configuration.
Nested repository targets are explicitly classified before support is claimed.
Submodule targets are explicitly classified before support is claimed.
Linked-worktree targets are explicitly classified before support is claimed.
Case-insensitive alias targets are explicitly classified before support is claimed.
UNC targets are explicitly classified before support is claimed.
Cloud-sync targets are explicitly classified before support is claimed.
Clone-with-active-writer targets are explicitly classified before support is claimed.
Other non-local targets are explicitly classified before support is claimed.
Core commands perform zero network access.
Schemas and conformance data required at runtime are bundled for offline use.
Human help is bundled for offline use.
M0 performs no update checks.
M0 emits no telemetry.
The tool does not claim to detect or protect all secrets in dossier content.
Evidence stores references and digests by default and never copies artifact bytes without a later explicit feature.
Uninstalling the CLI never removes .case-agent data.
Purge and retention automation are outside M0.
Offline operation never implies supply-chain verification, sandboxing, privacy certification, or protection from other local processes.

A claimed POSIX local profile creates target-directory temporaries and create-once files exclusively, uses the declared local rename primitive, fully reads and validates snapshots, proves termination before recovery, and distinguishes process-crash safety from power-loss durability.

A Windows local profile is not claimed until its specified same-volume temporary, CREATE_NEW, replacement, delete-sharing, process-identity, bounded-retry, and post-failure verification behavior is proven.
On Windows the frozen public CLI returns CASE_E_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE with process exit 10 until a real Windows local profile is proven.
The public support matrix lists only real platform profiles that pass the complete frozen corpus.
The host-neutral protocol claims only filesystem behavior proven by the active declared profile; a controlled-test adapter is test capability and never production-platform support.
Every normative executable requirement has every declared positive and negative direction covered by an actually executed discriminating vector.
Every conformance case is a recursively closed, schema-validated fixture_version 1 object with every contract field explicit.
Every content, stdin, stdout, stderr, prompt, and view reference resolves to a regular file inside the frozen corpus.
Every declared input content digest matches referenced bytes before execution.
Initial and expected tree paths are safe, unique, stable-ordered repository-relative paths.
Fresh repositories are populated without traversal, absolute, drive, UNC, backslash, link, reparse, alias, or duplicate-path escape.
Random IDs, clocks, retry timing, locale, process identity, environment, and platform behavior are fixed by deterministic adapters.
Every executed case denies and audits network access deterministically.
Sequential and grouped concurrent invocations execute the same dispatcher and workflows.
Invocation and expectation counts match exactly.
Concurrent allowed results are explicit and every concurrency group enforces exactly one success.

The frozen corpus executes every blocking initialization, JSON/schema/JCS, writer, retry, publication-fault, guard, evidence, handoff, submission, decision, version/internal, rehydration, platform-text/path, and offline family.
An explicit validator or fault mutation proves state-critical corruption turns a formerly passing vector red.
Mutating expected stdout, final tree, or derived view cannot be trusted as success and turns the oracle red.
Before adding a skill or second-host adapter, the baseline comparison covers competing writers, stale handoff acceptance, changed accepted artifacts, and evidence that no longer matches.

The baseline compares ordinary Markdown plus Git against the L0 reference CLI without a skill, using correct detection without false success as the primary metric and the specified burden measures as secondary metrics.
M0 advances only after detecting all four target failures with documented acceptable burden, and that result never justifies broader reliability claims.
M0 is not releasable until the normative L0 specification and schema projections are complete.
M0 is not releasable until every executable MUST has its required positive and negative fixtures.
M0 is not releasable until the full frozen corpus passes on every claimed real platform profile.
M0 is not releasable unless race tests produce exactly one successful conforming mutation.
M0 is not releasable if a direct-edit fixture can become green.
M0 is not releasable if stale-evidence fixtures can become green.
M0 is not releasable if stale-handoff fixtures can become green.
M0 is not releasable if stale-acceptance fixtures can become green.
M0 is not releasable if validator exceptions do not fail closed.
M0 is not releasable until the complete walking skeleton succeeds without network access.
M0 is not releasable until a context-loss run resumes from the bounded current view.
M0 is not releasable until the Markdown baseline comparison is recorded.

Release documentation makes no unsupported identity, audit, sandbox, enterprise, weak-model, or reliability claim, an independent review finds no spec/schema/CLI/fixture contradiction, and preview claims remain limited to demonstrated file-native, invariant, handoff, and exact platform-profile results.
